rationale: The book's core identification — 'the truth' = God's law/word as the covenant standard — is stated verbatim by its lead proof text (Ps 119:142, 'thy law is the truth') and corroborated by John 17:17 ('thy word is truth') and 2 John 4 (where 'walking in truth' is defined in the immediate context, 2 John 6, as walking after the commandments). The strongest counter, the mainstream Christocentric reading ('Jesus IS the truth,' John 14:6), does not materially contradict this core: the book affirms and explains the Christological data by its embodiment mechanism (Christ as 'the Torah embodied — the standard walking'), so both claims can be true of the same referent. Moreover, the common interpretation itself lists 'the truth as Scripture/the Word of God' as a common layer, meaning the counter is a broader umbrella rather than a rival core. The book explains the definite-article predication in the explicit definitional verses (law IS the truth; word IS truth) better than the Christocentric reading, which must treat those verses as secondary attributes rather than definitions. No supplied text is better explained by the counter in a way the book's core cannot accommodate; John 1:17's law/grace-and-truth contrast is the nearest candidate but was not part of the supplied evidence bundle and is answerable (the Greek lacks an adversative, and 'grace and truth' echoes the covenant pair of Exodus 34:6), so it remains a non-decisive objection.
book_core_identification: 'The truth' in Scripture refers to God's law/word — the divine covenant standard by which everything else is measured — such that Jesus' claim 'I am the truth' means He is that standard embodied in a person.
book_secondary_elaborations: Modern readers wrongly hear 'truth' as mere factual accuracy; Scripture defines it as the measure itself
The three titles of John 14:6 (way, truth, life) are one Torah-reality seen from three angles: the standard, the conduct, and the covenant-existence
The door imagery (word on the doorposts, blood on the doorposts) shows Christ as entrance 'by the word and by the blood'
The flaming sword of Genesis 3:24 is the word of God (Eph 6:17) guarding the way of life
The prosphatos ('freshly slain') etymology in Hebrews 10:20
'Unto the Father' rather than 'to heaven' as the destination of the way
strongest_counter_interpretation: The mainstream Christocentric reading: 'the truth' is God's self-revelation personally embodied in Jesus Christ — not primarily a body of law or text but the divine reality and saving revelation of God in a person, per John 14:6 ('I am the truth'), John 1:14, 17 ('full of grace and truth... grace and truth came through Jesus Christ'), and John 18:37. On this reading, verses calling the law or word 'truth' describe attributes or expressions of the deeper personal reality, and John 1:17 arguably contrasts the law (given by Moses) with the truth (come through Christ).
counter_core_identification: 'The truth' is God's revealed divine reality personified in Jesus Christ, of which Scripture, gospel, and law are expressions rather than the definition.
material_core_denial: The counter would materially deny the book's core only if it insisted that 'the truth' in John 14:6 names Christ's divine person in a way that excludes identification with God's law/standard — e.g., by reading John 1:17 as an explicit contrast between the law (Moses) and truth (Christ), so that truth cannot BE the law. As formulated in the supplied common interpretation, however, it does not make this exclusive claim; it includes 'Scripture/the word as truth' among its common layers.
counter_case: John 14:6 predicates 'the truth' of a person, not a legal code — the most natural surface reading is personal identification
John 1:14 locates truth in the incarnate Word: 'full of grace and truth'
John 1:17 sets 'the law was given by Moses' alongside 'grace and truth came by Jesus Christ,' which can be read as contrasting law with truth
John 18:37 has Jesus come to 'bear witness to the truth' as a divine reality confronting Pilate, not to a statute
The Spirit is called 'the Spirit of truth' (John 14:17; 15:26; 16:13; 1 John 5:6), suggesting truth as revealed divine reality broader than Torah
book_explanatory_advantages: Ps 119:142 and John 17:17 are explicit definitional predications ('thy law is the truth'; 'thy word is truth') — the book takes them as definitions; the counter must demote them to attributes

The book explains the definite article in John 14:6 ('the truth,' not 'a truth') by an antecedent scriptural definition the hearers already possessed, consistent with the book's demonstrated OT-first decoding method
2 John 4–6 defines 'walking in truth' as walking after the commandments, matching truth = the commanded standard
The book accounts for the Christocentric data rather than denying it: Christ is the truth because He is the standard embodied ('the law in the flesh'), so John 14:6 is explained, not explained away

The reading unifies the triad of John 14:6 via Proverbs 6:23 ('the commandment is a lamp; the law is light; reproofs of instruction are the way of life'), giving a single coherent structure: the truth defines the way, the way produces the life
It explains why sanctification is 'through thy truth' (John 17:17): the standard is the instrument of setting apart
counter_explanatory_advantages: Handles John 14:6's personal predication with zero mediating steps
Better fits John 1:14 and 18:37, where truth attaches to the incarnate person and his witness
Naturally accommodates the pneumatological texts ('the Spirit is the truth,' 1 John 5:6) that a strict truth=law equation must stretch to cover
If John 1:17 is read adversatively, it directly supports distinguishing truth from the Mosaic law
decisive_sources: Psalm 119:142 — 'thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth' (explicit definitional predication, the entry's printed proof text)
John 17:17 — 'Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth'
2 John 4 with 2 John 6 — 'walking in truth' defined as walking after the commandments
John 14:6 as explained by the book's embodiment mechanism (the standard become a person)
Proverbs 6:23 — commandment/lamp, law/light, way of life — unifying the triad
unresolved_objections: John 1:17's apparent contrast between the law given by Moses and the truth come through Christ is not addressed in the supplied chapter and remains the strongest textual friction, though it is answerable and was not part of the evidence bundle
The pneumatological texts (John 14:17; 16:13; 1 John 5:6 'the Spirit is the truth') are not accounted for by the chapter and fit the broader revelation reading more directly
Secondary elaborations (prosphatos = 'freshly slain,' the flaming sword as the word, tree = nation) rest on etymology or cross-symbol claims argued elsewhere and are weaker than the core
John 18:37–38 (witness to the truth before Pilate) is not treated in the chapter
